questions.text: The marked price of an article is Rs. 120. If the article is sold at a discount of 10%, 35% profit is realised. How much loss or profit will be made if it is sold for Rs. 30 less than the marked price?
questions.explanation:
The marked price of an article is Rs. 120

Selling price after 10% discount = Rs. 108

Since 35% profit is realised

⇒ Cost price of the article = 108/1.35 = Rs. 80

If it is sold for Rs. 30 less than the marked price, the selling price will be Rs. 90

∴ Profit percentage = [90 - 80] /80 = 12.5%

questions.text: If marked price of a washing machine including GST is Rs. 30800. The rate of GST is 12% and then there is a discount of 5%. If the shopkeeper is earning a profit of 10% in this transaction, then find the cost price of a washing machine.
questions.explanation:
Given:

The marked price of a washing machine including GST is Rs. 30800

The rate of GST is 12% and the discount percentage is of 5%

The shopkeeper gets the profit of 10% on this transaction

Formula Used:

SP = MP – discount

CP = SP × 100/ (100 + profit %)

Calculation:

The marked price of washing machine = Rs. 30800

According to the question

Rate of GST and discount allowed is 12% and 5% respectively

The marked price of a washing machine without GST rate

⇒ 30800 × 100/112 = Rs 27,500

A discount of 5% is also allowed

SP = MP – discount

⇒ SP = Rs. 27,500 – (27,500 × 5/100) = Rs. 26,125

Profit percentage = 10%

CP = SP × 100/ (100 + profit %)

⇒ Cost price of an machine = 26125 × 100/110 = Rs. 23750

Alternate Method

SP of the washing machine = CP × (110/100) = MP × (100/112) × (95/100)   

CP = 30800 × 95 × 10/(112 × 11) = Rs 23,750

∴ CP of the machine is Rs. 23750

questions.text: After a 25% initial discount on the marked price of an item, a shopkeeper offers a 20% additional discount on the discounted price. If the final sale price of the article is Rs. 600, then what is its marked price?
questions.explanation:
Given:

1st Discount = 25% of M.P

2nd Discount = 20% of 1st Discount

S.P = Rs. 600

Concept Used:

D = M.P × Rate of Discount 

Successive Discount = [a + b - (ab/100)]%

M.P = Marked Price, D = Discount, S.P = Selling Price

Calculation:

Let the marked price be x.

According to the question,

x × (75/100) × (80/100) = 600

⇒ x = (600 × 100 × 100)/(75 × 80)

⇒ x = 1000

∴ The Marked Price is Rs. 1000.

questions.text: The marked price of a headphone is Rs. 1400. A shopkeeper offers 20% discount on the net price and then again offers a discount of 12% on the reduced price. In the second offer, he offers a discount of 29% on the whole. Which is the better offer?

options.text: 20% and 12% successive discount for the customer
29% on the whole for the seller
20% and 12% successive discount for the selller

questions.explanation:
Calculation:

Case - 1

⇒ Marked price = 1400

⇒ First discount = 20%

⇒ S.P = 1400 – (20% of 1400) = 1120

⇒ Second discount = 12% on reduced price

⇒ Final S.P = 1120 – (12% of 1120) = 985.6

Case - 2

⇒ Marked price = 1400

⇒ Discount on whole = 29%

⇒ S.P = 1400 – (29% of 1400) = 994

∴ Case 1 is favorable for the customer and case - 2 is favorable for the seller

questions.text: Arun marked the water heater 40% above the cost price.  The ratio of cost price to selling price of a water heater is 10: 13.  Find the selling price of water heater if the difference between marked price and the selling price is 50?
questions.explanation:
Solution:
The ratio of cost price to selling price of a water heater is 10: 13.
Let the cost price be 10x and selling price be 13x.
Arun marked the water heater 40% above the cost price.  
Hence the marked price is 14x.
Given that difference between marked price and selling price is 50
That is 14x – 13x = 50 
x = 50 
hence the selling price is 13 ×  50 = 650.

questions.text: A shopkeeper buys a table marked at Rs. 4000 at two successive discounts of 20% and 15%. He spends Rs. 80 in transportation of the table and sells the table at Rs. 3220. Find the percentage profit earned by the shopkeeper.
questions.explanation:
Equivalent discount to two successive discounts of 20% and 15% = 20 + 15 - [20 × 15]/100 = 32%

⇒ Cost of the table after discount = 4000 × 0.68 = Rs. 2720

Since He spends Rs. 80 in transportation

⇒ Cost price of the table for shopkeeper = 2720 + 80 = Rs. 2800

Since he sells the table at Rs. 3220.

∴ Percentage profit earned by the shopkeeper = [3220 - 2800] /2800 = 15%

questions.text: A shopkeeper gives two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on surplus stock. Further, he also gives 5% extra discount on cash payment. If a person buys a shirt from the surplus stock and pays in cash, what overall discount percent will he get on the shirt?
questions.explanation:
Let the marked price of the shirt be Rs. 1000

⇒ Price after first discount

= Rs. 1000 – 20% of Rs. 1000

= Rs. 1000 – 200 = Rs. 800

⇒ Price after the second discount

= Rs. 800 – 10% of Rs. 800

= Rs. 800 – 80 = Rs. 720

⇒ Price after cash discount

= Rs. 720 – 5% of Rs. 720

= Rs. 720 – 36 = Rs. 684

⇒ Therefore, total discount

= Rs. 1000 – 684 = Rs. 316

Overall discount percent

= (316 / 1000) x 100 = 31.60%

∴ Discount is of 31.60%

questions.text: Shopkeeper purchased two different quality of sugar A and B in which A had price of Rs. 30/kg and B had price of 66.67% more than A and mixed both quality of sugar in equal amount.He sold 10 kg of prepared mixture at Rs. 500.What is the different in % of profit if he provide no discount and he provides the discount of Rs. 5/kg of selling the mixture?
questions.explanation:
For the cost price per kg of mixture,

Cost price of B = cost price of A + 66.67% of cost price of A = 30 + (2/3) × 30 = Rs. 50

Cost price of mixture = 30 × 0.5 + 50 × 0.5 = 15 + 25 = Rs. 40

[Here, 0.5 is quantity of sugar in mixture i.e. 500 grams]

For selling price per kg,

Selling price per kg = 500/10 = Rs.50

Profit = 50 – 40 = Rs. 10 per kg

% of profit = profit made/cost price = (10/40) × 100 = 25%

For discount,

Selling price after discount = 50 – 5 = Rs.45

Profit earn = discounted price – cost price = 45 – 40 = Rs. 5

% of profit = (5/40) × 100 = 12.5%

∴ % difference in profit = 25 – 12.5 = 12.5%

questions.text: Shailaja purchased a school bag with a price tag of Rs. 1220 in a sale where 25% discount was being offered on the tag price. She was given a further discount of 6%. What was the final amount paid by Shailaja?
questions.explanation:
Price tag is nothing but the Marked price(M.P.)

⇒ M.P. of the school  bag = Rs.1220

Price of the bag after a discount of 25% = 1220 – (25% of 1220)

⇒ Price of the bag after a discount of 25% =1220 – 305 = Rs.915

Price of the bag after a further discount of 6% = 915 – (6% of 915) = 915 – 54.9 = Rs.860.10

∴ Final amount paid by Shailaja = Rs.860.10

questions.text: After modifying the product, firm relaunch it by increasing the price by 20%. Due to targeted sales not achieved, the company decided to offer a discount of 12% on the product. If the current price of Product is Rs. 21,648. Find the price of the product before the relaunch.
questions.explanation:
Let the price of product before re launch = Rs. x,

For price increased by 20%,

Increased price of product = 1.2x

For price decreased by 12%,

Reduced price of product = 1.2x × 0.88 = 1.056x

For the original price of product,

⇒ 21648 = 1.056x

⇒ x = 21648/1.056

∴ Price of product before re launch = 21648/1.056 = Rs. 20,500
